images.title: Four parts, three creases
images.purpose: Show that folding the strip in half twice makes 4 equal parts of 1/4 unit, and that 3 parts together measure 3 × 1/4 = 3/4 unit.
images.composition: One long strip across the middle of the frame, with a bracket above part of it and a bracket below the whole.
images.exact_structure: One strip, 1 unit long, split by 3 grey #6B7280 creases into 4 exactly equal parts. The first 3 parts from the left filled teal #0072B2, the fourth part plain. Above the strip: one reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket over the first 3 parts. Below the strip: one grey bracket over the whole strip. The leftmost part carries a small label. Exactly 1 strip, 3 creases, 4 equal parts, 2 brackets.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
parts of unequal length, or a number of creases other than 3
images.takeaway: Count the parts, not the creases: each part is 1/4 unit.
images.description: A 1 unit strip with 3 creases making 4 equal parts of 1/4 unit; a bracket over 3 shaded parts reads 3 × 1/4 = 3/4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the creases and then the parts, and say which count names the unit.

image_decisions.why: One strip with 3 creases and 4 parts shows the unit one fourth and a length measured in it.
